#2742. The Worst Loss in Pelicans History

Winning in the NBA is hard; growing pains are always going to happen, especially with a franchise under a new coach and mentality. But after an embarrassing showing by a short-handed New Orleans Pelicans, more questions arose than answers. There is talent on the roster, but the fit may never be right for the team to be competitive.

With Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III out, the second game of a back-to-back on the road against Steph Curry, arguably the best shooter of all time, and Steve Kerr, one of the best coaches in NBA history. A perfect storm led to the Pelicans' worst loss in franchise history and raised a huge red flag for the rest of the season.

The 51-point blowout was an insult to injury, as Curry did not play for much of the fourth quarter.

Golden State had over 40% of its salary cap unavailable due to devastating injuries to Jimmy Butler (recovering from an ACL tear), Moses Moody (recovering from a patellar tendon tear), and Kristaps Porziņģis (dealing with a rare disorder that threatens his NBA career). They had three players with over 25 points: Curry, Brandin Podziemski, and Yaxel Lendeborg, who is a rookie, by the way.

Even though it is just one regular-season game out of 82, this is the Pelicans' third straight loss, and it raises a massive red flag for them moving forward. The first issue is finding rotations that actually work. With a roster that has major deficiencies, including a lack of shooting and length, coach Jamahl Mosley has to figure out a way to improve the team's spacing without sacrificing rim protection, which is easier said than done.

The team has shown small glimpses of winning basketball. It all starts on the defensive end for the Pelicans by creating turnovers and limiting opponents to one shot. This mitigates, to a certain extent, the lack of shooting on the roster by leveraging most players' ability to play downhill and attack the rim.

New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson (1) reacts during the fourth quarter against the Los Angeles Clippers at Intuit Dome. Photo Credit: Kiyoshi Mio, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect

The lack of accountability from the Pelicans has haunted the team for the last 10 years. Ever since Rajon Rondo left after only one season, the Pelicans have been adrift in their search for a true locker-room leader.

The leader of a team does not need to be its superstar. Many could argue that Draymond Green fills that role for the Warriors more than Curry does. This leader needs to be vocal with both the roster and the referees.

During Anthony Davis's time in New Orleans, his personality was better suited to a secondary role than to that of a leader who holds the team accountable. That is exactly why he was so successful during his championship run with the Lakers: without a doubt, LeBron James was the leader of that team.

During the Brandon Ingram-Zion Williamson era, both players were extremely young and less vocal. Some would argue that Ingram was more of a leader, but only because Williamson missed extended periods due to injuries.

When the team traded for CJ McCollum, he brought a more professional presence to the organization. However, with the number of injuries to their core players, the team was still set up for disappointment.

Currently, the team has one veteran presence. DeAndre Jordan has taken on a leadership and mentorship role for many of the young players, including Derik Queen. His playing time is nonexistent, so having a leader who is not on the court is not 100% effective, as he cannot call out the rest of the team on the same mistakes they make season in and season out.

These mistakes include a lack of spacing on the offensive end, playing great defense for 20 seconds of the shot clock only to leave the other team's best shooter wide open, and the killer for any team: playing great defense, forcing a contested shot, only for the offense to secure second-chance points.

New Orleans Pelicans guard Jordan Poole (3) as a time out is called against the Golden State Warriors during the third quarter at Chase Center. Photo Credit: Kelley L Cox, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect

But the question remains: after an atrocious loss and a third straight defeat, what player will call out the rest of the roster?

Five-time NBA champion and Hall of Famer, the late great Kobe Bryant, became famous in the latter years of his career for calling out teammates he felt were soft, once saying that he had seen their preparation, so why would he pass them the ball? He asked the equipment guy to take away all the players' sneakers who wore Kobe's because they were "Charming soft".

The Pelicans desperately need someone willing to hold teammates accountable, because talent alone has never been enough to build a winning culture. If the results don't show any improvement by the trade window, New Orleans may hold a fire sale on most of their roster, facing a dreaded rebuild.

#2740. Cleveland Browns 2027 mock draft: Help on defense and finally a QB

Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken finally delivered the answer on Wednesday to the question that has kept the NFL on edge since Sunday evening.

Deshaun Watson is indeed returning as the team's starting quarterback for this Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.

It was the only logical decision for Monken to make given that Watson helped the Browns to a 5-3 record before missing last week's overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints with a concussion.

Because this is Monken's first year in Cleveland, a town where manufactured quarterback debates go to thrive, he seemed genuinely puzzled on Wednesday about why he would need to make a formal announcement about the starting quarterback:

"I don't even know why I have to say it publicly, because it's really only our business in terms of who's going to play and who's not going to play. But I mean, he played well enough to earn to still be our starter."

Even though the Browns now have their starting quarterback established for the rest of this season, there are still going to be questions about what they will do in 2027.

Watson's contract is up at the end of this season, and no matter what happens the rest of the way, the Browns really need to move on from the most controversial quarterback that has ever been on the roster.

That leaves Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, both destined for careers as backup quarterbacks, and rookie Taylen Green, whose future role in the NFL has yet to be determined.

So the Browns will need a new starting quarterback – or at least a rookie that projects to actually be a starting quarterback – which should lead general manager Andrew Berry to select one in the 2027 NFL Draft.

Berry will be holding a pair of first-round selections come draft, both Cleveland's and the one received from the Los Angeles Rams as part of the Myles Garrett trade, but neither appears as if they will be at the top of the draft.

Which means that Berry will have to either work a trade or wait and see who might fall to him on draft night.

That is the path that The Athletic's Nick Baumgardner sees Berry taking in this Round 1 mock draft, with Baumgardner projecting that the Browns will be selecting at No. 15 and No. 19 overall.

With quarterbacks Drew Mestemaker (Miami at No. 3) and CJ Carr (New York Jets at No. 6) off the board, but with (gasp!) Arch Manning still in the green room, the Browns select Clemson defensive end Will Heldt with their first pick:

Big enough, at 6-6, 260, to be an edge setter, Heldt is also crafty enough with his hands to rack up pass-rush wins. His build somewhat resembles that of Aidan Hutchinson.

Heldt is in his second season with the Tigers after playing two years at Purdue. In 46 career games so far, he has 146 tackles, 19.5 sacks, and 37.5 tackles for loss.

Four picks later at No. 19, Berry finally ends the suspense, and the Browns select quarterback Darian Mensah from Miami:

The College Football Playoff — assuming Miami gets in, as it should — figures to be a huge stretch for Mensah. The Hurricanes' star has the potential to be a top-10 pick, but he still needs to show more consistency, both downfield and as a processor when facing high-level teams. His arrow is firmly pointed up, though.

Mensah is in his first season with the Hurricanes after playing one season at Tulane (2024) and one at Duke (2025). In helping Miami to an 8-1 record, Mensah is completing 76.8 percent of his passes for 2,694 yards, 28 touchdowns, and just two interceptions.

Two first-round picks and the Browns add an impact player on defense and take their latest and greatest shot at fixing the quarterback situation.

What do you think? Would you be happy with those picks, or would you prefer that Berry goes in a different direction? Let everyone know in the comments!

#2736. Warriors star Steph Curry claps back at weird podcast criticism of wife Ayesha Curry

HOUSTON - Stephen Curry was evidently none too pleased with social-media chatter around wife Ayesha Curry's first feature-film leading role in the romantic comedy "Second Chance Holiday."

A clip from the film, featuring Ayesha Curry giving an on-screen kiss to co-star Matthew Daddario, went viral this past week and served as fodder for a wide variety of podcasts. Former NBA All-Star Gilbert Arenas and former Golden State Warriors backup Nick Young held a 17-minute segment Saturday on the kiss, with Arenas saying "the only blemish in the (Curry) family is the wife." Media personality Emmanuel Acho also devoted a good bit of airtime to the topic.

On Wednesday, Curry took to Instagram for a notably pointed response.

"I've been hearing a lot of noise, and usually the noise doesn't bother me, doesn't bother Ayesha, but this one in particular - when you're trying to step on the accomplishments of my wife, and obviously needing podcast tapings and topics and giving opinions on somebody else's wife - Nick, (Gilbert), Emmanuel, and anybody else who feels the need to want to have to jump in and give an opinion on something you don't really know about and kinda speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they're allowed and what they're not allowed to do, even the ignorance behind how acting works," Curry said, cycling through an array of mocking faces.

"Obviously, I tried to laugh this one off," he continued. "But something needs to be said. And anytime Ayesha Curry shows up in your headline, I kindly suggest you just give the happy hands, the congratulations, and maybe, just maybe, the apology can be as loud as y'all leading y'all shows with this topic."

The video was clearly filmed handheld, at the spur of the moment. A source with direct knowledge of Curry's thinking said that the video response wasn't planned or organized by his team in any way, and came directly from Curry.

The majority of Arenas and Young's content centered on the odd idea of Ayesha Curry potentially bringing a negative perception to the Curry family due to her acting career, visibility and independent personal success, a narrative that has existed on social media for years as her husband has simultaneously become one of the most famous athletes on the planet. Curry has increasingly dipped into the Hollywood space in recent years, starring in the animated film "GOAT" and directing the short documentary "The Baddest Speechwriter of All" this year.

Back on the court, Curry has led the Warriors to an 8-3 start in 2026-27, averaging 30.6 points, 4.1 rebounds and 4.3 assists in one of the hottest early-season stretches of his career.

#2731. Jazz star Lauri Markkanen set to miss at least a month with fractured hand

The early-season injuries in the NBA keep piling up as the Utah Jazz announced that forward Lauri Markkanen was set to miss at least a month with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand.

It's a brutal blow for a Jazz team that looked ready to contend for a playoff spot in the Western Conference after four straight losing seasons. Last year, the Jazz traded for Jaren Jackson Jr., but he played just three games before getting shut down with an injury. They had also lost starting center Walker Kessler to injury after just five games, and Markkanen himself was limited to just 42 games.

Yet, there was optimism building around the Jazz heading into this season. Even with Kessler now on the Lakers, the Jazz had Markkanen and Jackson Jr. healthy to pair with breakout guard Keyonte George and dynamic rookie Darryn Peterson. Ace Bailey and Isaiah Collier were likely to be impactful young options off the bench, and the play-in seemed like a bare minimum in Utah.

Jackson played four games before tearing the MCL in his right knee. Jusuf Nurkic, who was set to replace Kessler at center, hasn't made his season debut yet as he battles a foot injury, and Keyonte George sprained his ankle over the weekend. Both George and Markkanen sat out Utah's game on Tuesday before it was revealed how serious Markkanen's injury was.

The 29-year-old has played in eight of the Jazz's 11 games this season and was averaging 18.0 points, 6.8 rebounds, and 2.0 assists while shooting a disappointing 38.9% from the field. With his struggles and the mounting injuries, the Jazz have put together just the 21st-ranked defense and 29th-ranked offense, which has led to the 26th-best net rating in the league. With a record of 1-10, it's not at all the start the team envisioned.

With Markkanen sidelined for the next month, the Jazz might continue to start Josh Green at small forward, but Markkanen's usage will likely be spread to shooting guard Darryn Peterson and power forward Ace Bailey. In Tuesday's loss to the Heat, Peterson scored 25 points on 10-of-19 from the field with four rebounds and four assists, while Bailey scored 23 points on 10-for-15 from the field to go along with seven rebounds and two assists. Their development will be a silver lining amidst all the injuries for the Jazz.

However, by the time Markkanen and Jackson Jr. return, the improvement of Peterson and Bailey may not be enough to save what looks to be another lost season.

#2726. Fantasy Basketball Rankings (9-cat leagues): Early risers and fallers of the 2026-27 NBA season

We're into Week 4, and below is my 9-cat riser and faller list through Week 3, featuring five risers and five fallers. Ranks are my rest-of-season 9-cat projections, not a summary of who's performed best so far. Stats are through Nov. 9 (about 8–11 games played per player), so sample sizes are still small.

Mitchell has become one of the NBA's top playmakers. Not bad for a guy who went around pick 120 during draft season. His 8.5 assists a night rank fifth in the league, with a potential 14.8 assists per game. That's just the passing. His shot volume has almost doubled, boosting his scoring to over 16 points per game, along with 2.2 3s. And he's still getting steals, averaging over 1 per outing. The only knock to his game is his free-throw shooting. Playing high minutes on a team with little creation outside of Giannis Antetokounmpo and sometimes Pelle Larsson, Mitchell has real staying power as a PG anchor. He ranks near the top-50 in both points and 9-cat through three weeks.

It's a luxury for the Timberwolves to have a player of Ayo's caliber to step in for Anthony Edwards. He's been a model of efficiency for years and has been impactful whenever he saw an increase in minutes and opportunity. That tracks with what we've seen from Dosunmu this season. Dosunmu is shooting 52% from the field and 89% at the line, scoring 18.1 points, grabbing 4.9 rebounds, and adding 4.1 assists, while still tacking on 1.9 3s and 1.3 steals in 31 minutes. As long as Edwards is out, Ayo is a top-40 player in 9-cat and top-60 in High Score, averaging over 36 fantasy points per night.

Health is wealth. So far, Zion is pacing to last season's numbers — similar shot volume, but excelling in the paint. Zion is fourth in the league in points in the paint, averaging 14.1 per game.  Zion is shooting 63% while getting to the line 7.2 times a game. Bully ball. Also, his steal rate is pacing to a career high, with over 2 per game. That number is bound to regress, but the combination of his high FG and steal rates, improving free-throw percentage (76.4) and scoring over 20 ppg with 5 boards is what's elevated him to 22nd in 9-cat, 34th in points and 43rd in High Score. I'd sell high in each format except for High Score.

Smith is in the midst of a breakout campaign. Through 11 games, everything is clicking for the third pick of the 2022 NBA Draft. He's averaging 17.0 points, 6.5 boards, 2.7 3s, 50% shooting, 45% on 3s and 86% at the line. There's even been a boost in assists to almost 3 per game. I think it's more of a testament to Fred VanVleet's leadership and opening up the floor for the supporting cast to operate more freely. Smith's success has been one of the biggest surprises three weeks into the season. A couple more weeks of this level of play and he might be able to fetch something real on the fantasy trade market.

Bridges is definitely a riser in 9-cat leagues. He's currently 27th, averaging 15-7-3 with 45/33/87 shooting splits. He's also getting over a steal per contest. Now, while those numbers are solid, I don't trust he'll be able to keep this up all season. The supporting cast outside of Booker has been dreadful. I expect their improvements will alter some of Bridges' success to date. Bridges' rebounding numbers are pacing to the best of his career, as is his low turnover rate. But top-30 (and top 70 in High Score and points formats) is too good to be true. Sell, sell, sell.

What happened to this man? He's become Toumani Camara; 67% of Bane's shots have come from beyond the arc. He's still knocking down 3.6 a game, but he's shooting 37% overall and 36% from 3. His turnovers are up to 2.6 per contest and he's providing just 2.4 assists for a guy who went 53rd in ADP. His 15 shots per game is consistent with his past couple of seasons. The main difference is the shot diet — chucking 3s, taking half the amount of 2-point FGs and not going to the line nearly enough — a recipe for disaster and it's why he's 136th in 9-cat.

This one hurts, and the culprit is minutes. Ware is down to 17.3 a game after playing 22.2 last season, and 8.6 points and 6.9 rebounds on 40% shooting won't cut it. He's only played more than 20 minutes in two of 11 games this season. Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins isn't giving him much leeway, similar to how Spoelstra handled him, likely because of the same mental lapses that frustrated coaches in Miami. I hyped him up, but that ADP in the high 70s always looked a bit sus considering he's still behind Myles Turner. It's a long season, but I understand if fantasy managers want to drop him.

Harden looks old. His scoring and assist numbers have fallen off a cliff — he's shooting just 36% from the field and averaging 5.7 assists (down significantly from his career averages). Turnovers are still an issue at 3.0 per game, which hurts in multiple categories, and the free-throw attempts have dropped to just 4.8 a game. There's legitimate reason to be concerned about how he's moving and producing, but I still see him as a buy-low. This feels more like an early-season slump than a full-on panic. If you can acquire him at a discount, now is the time to try.

A season ago, Rollins was a 32-minute guy averaging 17 points. Now he's playing 23 minutes and putting up 10.7 points on 38% shooting and 67% from the line and, more importantly, was passed on the depth chart by Brayden Burries. I have him 135th, but I'm giving him some grace in my latest rankings, expecting he'll turn it around somewhat — even if he's coming off the bench. He's much closer to a top-120 player than to 200, which is roughly where he sits in 9-cat through three weeks.

Six points a game on 33% shooting. That's the line, and it's ugly. Bridges put up 14.4 points on 49% shooting last season, so outside of his availability, he's giving fantasy managers nothing. I haven't found a good reason for it yet. He's playing 26 minutes a night with no offensive confidence and minimal stocks to save him on defense. I have him 134th, which is generous. #2722. Duke Tobin sends out 'not comfortable' head coach Zac Taylor to explain Bengals' trade-deadline snafu with Eagles

Zac Taylor almost certainly had little to nothing to do with the trade-deadline snafu on Tuesday in which the Cincinnati Bengals backed out of an agreed-upon deal with the Philadelphia Eagles.

On Wednesday, the Bengals' head coach took the podium to discuss the topic despite declaring that he was "not comfortable" doing so. He said he did it at the behest of director of player personnel and de facto general manager Duke Tobin.

Per Taylor, Tobin is "really apologetic." To be clear, that came from Taylor's mouth, not Tobin's.

"Obviously, we tried something yesterday," Taylor said. "Duke was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me of how he wanted this portrayed. I'm not comfortable doing it, but I'm going to do what he asked.

"We did make an effort to kind of put some depth in there in place of Cashius [Howell]. As we got into it, obviously it was going to be a little more costly than we initially anticipated. He's really apologetic about it and wants to make clear: Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our end."

In case you missed it, the Bengals had an agreement with the Eagles in place to acquire edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie prior to Tuesday's trade deadline. The Bengals need depth at the position due to a wrist injury that placed Howell on injured reserve.

In the agreed upon deal, the Bengals would've sent a sixth-round pick to the Eagles and received Ebiketie in return. But it turns out the deal came at a significantly higher cost, which the Bengals' front office apparently didn't realize when it made the agreement.

Per the NFL's compensatory picks mechanisms, the Bengals would've also had to forfeit a third-round compensatory pick to acquire Ebiketie. So in essence, they would have parted with a third-round pick and a sixth-round pick to acquire a backup pass rusher.

It's a price that's prohibitive and one the Bengals reportedly didn't realize until Over the Cap's self-proclaimed "Compensatory Picks Guy™" Nick Korte pointed it out on social media.

Korte's analysis picked up traction among traditional NFL media, and only then did the Bengals back out of the deal, having realized its true cost.

This was all reported Tuesday, and Taylor was left to confirm it with media on Wednesday.

This is not Taylor's job. He's a head football coach. He's not supposed to be tasked with knowing the complex mechanics of NFL trades or the league's compensatory pick system, and he's not the one who pulled the trigger on the agreement with the Eagles.

Those responsibilities lie with the player personnel arm of Cincinnati's front office, which is run by Tobin. The mistake was an embarrassment for Tobin's department that played out across sports media on Tuesday.

On Wednesday, Tobin sent out Taylor to face the music.

#2718. Lauri Markkanen injury update could have major fallout for Utah Jazz

The Utah Jazz hoped to be part of the Western Conference playoff race this season after years of rebuilding. But those plans have gone horribly awry during the opening few weeks of the 2026-27 NBA campaign, and getting back on track just became even more difficult after a sobering update involving star Lauri Markkanen.

Markkanen is expected to miss at least a month of action, the Jazz announced on Nov. 11, after suffering a right hand injury during the team's loss to the Dallas Mavericks last Friday. Markkanen is the latest key Jazz player to be sidelined, and the mounting absences have left Utah tied for the NBA's worst record at 1-10 entering Wednesday's matchup against the Orlando Magic.

Here's more on Markkanen's injury status and what it means for the Jazz's hopes of reaching the postseason.

NBA: Kon Knueppel's latest injury setback could be crushing blow for Hornets

Markkanen has been diagnosed with two nondisplaced fractures in his right hand and will be re-evaluated in four weeks. The good news is a nondisplaced fracture is considered less severe than a displaced fracture, in which the bones are no longer in proper alignment. A non-displaced fracture generally doesn't require surgery.

The 29-year-old forward had already been playing through a sprained right wrist as the Jazz were hit hard with injuries during the first month of the NBA season. An initial X-ray did not reveal the fracture, according to ESPN, but Markkanen underwent scans that revealed more damage after returning to Utah in recent days.

The Jazz were already teetering to start the 2026-27 season because of injuries, and they've lost 10 of their first 11 games. Utah watched Jaren Jackson Jr. go down for at least two months with a knee injury, while center Jusuf Nurkic has yet to appear in a game this season because of a toe injury. Guard Keyonte George has also been dealing with a sprained ankle and did not play in Tuesday's loss to the Miami Heat.

That leaves rookie Darryn Peterson as the only player from the Jazz's expected Opening Night starting lineup currently available entering Wednesday.

Utah was already struggling with Markkanen in the lineup, and losing its most reliable offensive weapon only makes an uphill climb steeper. His ability to score at all three levels, stretch defenses and create matchup problems is central to everything the Jazz want to do offensively. The timing is just brutal. A team that entered the season hoping to take a step forward is suddenly staring at the possibility of another year buried near the bottom of the Western Conference.

The injury could also create bigger-picture questions for the franchise. The Jazz resisted opportunities to trade Markkanen when his value was arguably at its peak, believing he would be the centerpiece of their return to contention. Now, with Utah off to a disastrous start and its roster ravaged by injuries, the mission is simply to keep the season from slipping away before Markkanen can return.

If this season ends as disastrously as it has started, the Jazz could revisit assumptions that have guided their moves to this point, including whether their current timeline and roster construction around Markkanen remain the right path forward.

Markkanen was averaging 18 points and 6.8 rebounds per game through eight games for the Jazz this season. He was shooting just 38.9% from the floor, which is the worst mark of his career. Markkanen averaged 26.7 points on 47.7% shooting during the 2025-26 season.

#2717. Cardinals Reveal Final Decision on Carson Beck’s Week 10 Status

Beck is officially making his debut as a starting QB in the NFL. Getty

The 3-6 Arizona Cardinals are heading into a week 10 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams facing mounting issues.

Arizona is already heading into the week without WR Michael Wilson, as well as an uncertain status surrounding C Hjalte Froholdt and others.

The major conversation this week has been at quarterback, however. This comes as incumbent starter Gardner Minshew II battles through a potentially serious injury. The general expectation has been that rookie Carson Beck will take the starting reigns in week 10, but no official confirmation came before Wednesday.

GettyBeck is officially making his debut as a starting QB in the NFL.

Head coach Mike LaFleur officially announced that the rookie is starting in week 10 during a press conference. The accompanying news is that Minshew will need surgery on his elbow injury. This is unfortunate for Minshew, but it clears the way for what was inevitable regardless.

The final eight games of the Cardinals' season will seemingly serve as an audition for the Miami product. Beck, 24, was a third-round pick in April for the Cardinals. The organization – including LaFleur – clearly believes in the Florida native to a high degree.

Beck's journey to becoming the starting QB hasn't been a seamless one despite the belief. He was held out of preseason action following the first contest due to a back issue. The subsequent result was sitting behind both Jacoby Brissett and Minshew prior to week nine against the Seattle Seahawks.

Now, the stage is Beck's to prove that he is the franchise guy for the Cardinals.

The Cardinals are asking a great deal out of Beck, particularly when contextualizing the help around him.

Arizona's wide receiver core is down to Semi Fehoko, Reggie Virgil, and Devin Duvernay. Jeremiyah Love will miss at least the next three weeks during his IR stint. Bam Knight is still in concussion protocol. The offensive line is in disarray as well, with Elijah Wilkinson and Isaac Seumalo positioning to be the only players within the group to start in every game.

Beck will have megastar Trey McBride at his disposal, but there isn't much permeating outside of the all-world pass catcher.

The upcoming matchups are also daunting for Beck. Los Angeles is trotting out an elite defensive line duo in Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. This is an immediate challenge for a rookie quarterback sitting behind a makeshift offensive line.

After this, the Cardinals travel to take on the Kansas City Chiefs. While Kansas City isn't as explosive from a pass rushing perspective, they are a relatively stingy defense overall.

The final six games will give Beck cleaner opportunities to prove himself as the future in Arizona. Upcoming matchups include porous units in the New York Jets and Las Vegas Raiders.

Until those days come, Beck will take on immediate daunting tests against challenging opponents. The Cardinals are taking on the Rams on Sunday afternoon at 2:25 P.M. MST from State Farm Stadium in Glendale.

#2715. 5 final observations for the 49ers following Raiders win and trade deadline

The San Francisco 49ers are coming off an eventful few days following their 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders and the trade deadline, where the team added Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen after trading for DeForest Buckner last week.

Now, the 49ers are set for the second half of the season with two new veterans in the fold, as they await several injury updates for this weekend's game against the Dallas Cowboys.

San Francisco was still banged up offensively against the Raiders, playing without Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans, but they still put up 38 points. Meanwhile, the defense continued to shine, creating five turnovers that sealed the deal for the Raiders.

Here are five observations from after the trade deadline following the Raiders win.

We've heard Kyle Shanahan talk about 'trust' when referencing Jordan Watkins, and we really saw that come out this past weekend, as the second-year wideout had his best game with four catches for 86 yards and a touchdown.

Watkins has paced the 49ers wide receivers in snaps with Mike Evans out, leading the team in the Washington, Atlanta, and Las Vegas games. That wasn't the case before that, though, as Watkins had been behind Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing in addition to San Francisco's top receivers in the weeks prior.

But now, post trade deadline, it feels like he could be in the top group for the 49ers until Mike Evans returns, joining Keenan Allen and Deebo Samuel. With this group of receivers, Watkins and Demarcus Robinson can play the vertical role, which means they're live for big plays every week.

We saw one of those come down last weekend with Watkins's 37-yard touchdown grab. On the season, he's now averaging 22.6 yards per catch. That trust is finally starting to pay off.

The 49ers have made it a goal to get Jaden Dugger on the field in a variety of roles this year. Dugger played 12 defensive snaps against Las Vegas, with only three coming in the box. 5 came on the line of scrimmage, while four were in the slot.

He's been a tackling machine, but also got a pick-six this past weekend. There were initial questions on usage for Dugger coming into the NFL as a Day 3 rookie, but he's been a fit everywhere.

Against Atlanta, Dugger played 31 snaps, with a ton coming on the line of scrimmage. With Dre Greenlaw out against Washington, he was much more of a full-time linebacker. Back in Week 5, he played 47 defensive snaps, with 16 being in the slot or on the line.

The snap count might dwindle with Upton Stout getting fully healthy and less need in the nickel, but Dugger has been a pleasant surprise so far this year in his usage.

DeForest Buckner was welcomed to the Bay Area and instantly played the most snaps of any defensive tackle against Las Vegas. He was on the field for 34 of the 50 defensive snaps, recording two pressures while Osa Odighizuwa had three.

Buckner was one of the most-played linemen in the NFL in Indianapolis, ranking in the top five in snap count. The 49ers will look to rotate him more than Indianapolis did, but it's clear he's going to have a big role, and the need was only further exacerbated by Gracen Halton's injury.

The 49ers seemed pretty adamant on adding a wide receiver, and even in his current state, Keenan Allen seems to fit what the team wants with his separation and blocking skills.

But with him in the fold, the future of the 49ers wide receiver room this season got more interesting. San Francisco seems to be getting Deebo Samuel back this weekend. They also should get Mike Evans in the coming weeks, while De'Zhaun Stribling is expected back in the regular season.

Then, there's Demarcus Robinson and the emerging Jordan Watkins alongside punt returner Jacob Cowing.

The first question comes with the starting group. When Evans, and really Stribling is back, will the 49ers rely on Allen still? And then, who is the odd man out of the group?

San Francisco will have Allen, Evans, Samuel, Stribling, Robinson, Watkins, and Cowing as their receivers then. They likely don't dress seven guys. Cowing has not been good as a receiver, but has maintained the punt return job. Does that go elsewhere and he's the odd man out? Or will the 49ers make a different move?

A lot of the 49ers focus on offense has been about the passing game, with Brock Purdy enjoying a career year and Mike Evans shining in his first season in the Bay.

But the 49ers run game has sneakily been elite this year from an efficiency perspective. The 49ers are seventh in yards per game (135.3) and seventh in yards per attempt (4.6). They're also third in EPA per rush and first in rushing success rate, so they've really turned things around in the run game.

San Francisco has adapted to the two-headed monster with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black, whose efficiency has risen in recent weeks. The offensive line has done a good job overall, and the Niners are quite balanced offensively.

That's a big sign for the coming weeks as the passing game still works through injuries, with the 49ers having their hardest stretch of the schedule coming up.

#2709. The Suns need to search for another scorer alongside Booker

With the season off to a slow start, many Suns fans have expressed frustration with the team, myself included. Whether it's how the starting lineup fits, the lack of cohesion on defense, the lack of a second star, or frustration with shooting percentages, there's something for someone to pick at and be mad about. For a team that was supposed to build on last year's success, it hasn't looked that bright just yet. They have shown in spurts that they can be this solid, but ultimately their shortcomings seem to overpower their positives.

Injuries to the team's frontcourt at the start of the year forced the Suns into a situation they may not have been as prepared for, and it has ultimately cost them. Then you add Jordan Goodwin being out and missing his hustle and rebounding, and there seem to be some issues. Especially when you look at the fact that in two games, Devin Booker has dropped over 30 points and the team has lost by a landslide; in this recent game vs. the Spurs and the one last week against the Trail Blazers, Booker was on and showed he can be that number one option for this team. He can hunt his shots, find them, and, most importantly, he is not washed.

Sadly, in both of those games, Booker had no one else show up offensively to help him. This is where the main problem comes into play, as the Suns' owner, Mat Ishbia, wants to win a championship, and one with Booker at the helm. Unfortunately, when your second-highest-paid player is the same position and functions best in the same role as your 1A star, you have a problem, and that is where Jalen Green comes into play.

Now it's not all Green's fault, since they're asking him to play a role he's never played in his career, and he's not too bad at it. Yes, he turns the ball over a lot when he mishandles it, but he can make some nice passes to create plays. The problem is that since he always has to make the pass, he also wants to hunt his shot when others are out. That doesn't work for Green, though, because it forces contested looks or shots, disrupting the team's rhythm. His averages this year clearly show this: his worst in six years.

Can he be a good player? For sure, but it depends on whether he can play a role he won't succeed in on a team that needs a true playmaker and facilitator. That will not help Booker and has proven to be the case this year. Will the Suns regret trading Green, though? No, because the fit was never going to work with how they're constructed, with Booker in the same role as Green.

So how does one get this second star in Phoenix, you may ask, right? Well, that goal may be one of the bigger obstacles for this team, since they lack draft capital. Remember that 2033 pick that the Suns traded for Miles Bridges? That was the team's most valuable asset, and yet they traded it the day they could for someone who, at best, would be the third offensive option.

Your assets are either Dillon Brooks, Miles Bridges, Mark Williams, or Jalen Green. Their value isn't enough to get you anything relevant for the next step. For everyone clamoring for Kyrie Irving, Anthony Davis, and Darius Garland, those players will cost a decent amount of pick value to acquire. With Green basically looking like a glorified six-man for the Suns in his best role, how would that trade value get boosted enough for other teams to see him as a positive?

That is why, sadly, this hunt for that second star may have to wait on Khaman Maluach's development. The big man has looked solid since moving into his bench role, and with more development this year, he can truly set himself up to take those next steps toward becoming a top-tier big man. This year, it seems like the team is trying to figure out new roles for the players we have and then make a playoff run. The offseason will focus on adding a second star player and freeing up time for this big-man duo to cement themselves as the true starter and backup.

At this point, I do think waiting that long is just not going to be beneficial. At this rate, we have seen that the true "second option" cannot be that, given his new role as the point guard. Brooks has to step up, and even though he can do it, the Suns should not be living and dying by his catch-and-shoot three for this season to be impactful. In his best role as the best defender, Brooks should be the third or fourth offensive option.

The game plan for the Suns seems tough, but there may be some light at the end of the tunnel. Even though we are just around 10 games in, there are clear issues that need to be addressed before the trade deadline. Some of them are even as early as next week, but time will tell if they make those adjustments or stand pat until they can actually pivot in a direction. With all that said, though, one thing is clear: if the Suns want another chance at a championship with Booker, they need another top-tier scoring option.

#2704. NFL news, live updates: Browns to start Deshaun Watson in Week 10; Vikings trade for QB Kirk Cousins

The 2026 NFL trade deadline is officially in the rearview mirror. Here's what you missed:

The biggest news of the day — the Minnesota Vikings have traded for Kirk Cousins in a reported deal with the Las Vegas Raiders, sending a third-round pick to Vegas in exchange for the vet. The move reunites Cousins with the Vikings, for whom he last played in 2023 before suffering a torn Achilles, and gives Minnesota some much-needed support at quarterback following Monday night's abysmal loss under Carson Wentz.

The Jacksonville Jaguars kicked off the NFL trade news cycle for the week with a splash move to bolster the secondary, sending a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons in exchange for Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III. They continued adding on defense throughout the day, also acquiring Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints and former first-round pick Jordan Davis in a blockbuster deal with the Philadelphia Eagles.

The Indianapolis Colts were another team to watch ahead of the trade deadline, with star running back Jonathan Taylor at the crux of it all. But as was first reported by NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the Colts did not trade Taylor ahead of Tuesday's deadline. The Colts did, however, trade wide receiver Josh Downs, who gets a fresh start with the Kansas City Chiefs and quarterback Patrick Mahomes.

Now, with all of that officially a wrap, it's time to gear up for Week 10.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more ahead of Week 10.

After a great deal of speculation was made that Jonathan Taylor could be moved ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Indianapolis Colts are reportedly standing pat.

The team will not trade him ahead of the deadline, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Tuesday afternoon.

Pelissero reported that the Colts had received multiple offers for Taylor of a second-round pick-plus, but instead, the team will move forward with him as a foundational piece within the locker room as they look to rebuild.

Riley Patterson will kick for the Ravens this week in their Monday Night Football matchup with the Chargers, according to the NFL Network's Mike Garafolo. Patterson spent the past two seasons with the Dolphins, but was released last month.

The Patriots will be playing the Lions in Munich, Germany, on Sunday.

Running back TreVeyon Henderson did not practice on Wednesday, and with an upcoming flight across the pond, the team has already ruled him out.

Henderson was listed on the injury report as dealing with an illness. The running back revealed last Friday that he recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms." Henderson was hospitalized, but has said that test results have been positive and reassuring.

Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson also didn't practice on Wednesday due to a knee injury, but has not yet been ruled out, though he is expected to miss a few weeks.

Sean McVay delivered a mix bag of news Wednesday regarding injuries to the team's top two receivers.

Davante Adams could be back sooner than expected from a hamstring injury, potentially in Week 13 vs. the Chiefs. Puka Nacua, meanwhile, will remain sidelined for a "significant period of time" with knee and toe injuries.

Etienne has been out since Week 3 due to a hamstring injury and has since been on injured reserve.

His return to practice opens his 21-day window to return to action, meaning the Saints have three weeks to activate him to the 53-man roster or shut him down for the season.

Skattebo missed Sunday's win over the Eagles coming out of the team's bye week. The running back practiced this week, which sets him up for a return Thursday night against the Commanders.

McCarthy was sacked five times in the game and suffered a rib injury that briefly took him out of action. He would return and finished 12-for-19 for 127 yards passing.

"I feel really good," McCarthy said this week. "Obviously, Sunday, it's football, it's a physical game, but just credit to the athletic training staff, getting me back to feeling really good as quick as possible."

The 49ers acquired Keenan Allen ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline because of the various injuries the team has at the position.

San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said on Wednesday that Mike Evans remains week-to-week due to an Achilles injury. At this point, he has not been added to IR, so Evans could suit up this week against the Cowboys, but he is starting the week by not practicing.

Shanahan added that currently there is no timeline for Evans' return.

The Rams are expected to be without star wide receiver Puka Nacua for more than a month after suffering two knee sprains in the team's most recent game.

Nacua, who would normally be added to IR to free up a roster spot, won't be, according to head coach Sean McVay. L.A. is still expecting Nacua to miss extended time, but NFL teams are only allowed eight player activations from IR per season.

If Nacua gets added, with the intention of activating him in December, he would take up an activation from another player that the Rams were planning on activating, which would rule them out for the year.

L.A. currently has WR Davante Adams, G Justin Dedich, DT Poona Ford and DE Kobie Turner on IR and the Rams likely want to be able to activate all of them later this year. Los Angeles has already used four activations with EDGE Myles Garrett, TE Terrance Ferguson, OT Keagan Trost and RB Ronnie Rivers.

The 49ers acquired Keenan Allen ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline to help bolster the banged-up wide receiver room.

The only problem is that Allen could still miss time this season. Kyle Shanahan acknowledged to reporters on Wednesday that the veteran wideout could still face league discipline this season stemming from his DUI in August.

According to the current CBA, a violation of the league's substance-abuse policy, which would include a DUI, comes with a minimum three-game suspension. Additionally, Allen's BAC was so high that the league can increase the suspension if it so chooses.

The league has reportedly been waiting for the DUI case against Allen to play out legally before issuing the suspension.

At 3-6, and with a rash of injuries — including one to their most recent QB1 — the Arizona Cardinals are turning to rookie Carson Beck.

Arizona benched and then traded Jacoby Brissett. His replacement, Gardner Minshew, suffered a UCL injury this past week in Seattle during a loss to the Seahawks.

In their absence, the No. 65 overall pick in this year's draft is getting the nod in the desert.

Beck will make his first career NFL start on Sunday when the Los Angeles Rams come to town, head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday. The former Georgia and Miami star will be tasked with moving the ball against a defense that features premier edge rusher Myles Garrett and stout defensive tackle Aaron Donald. Beck will have to do so with a thin receiving corps.

Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy announced on Wednesday that the team is opening the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Derrick Harmon.

The 23-year-old defender has been sidelined because of a sprained foot he suffered against the Bengals in Week 4. In limited action this season, he has 12 tackles, including 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble.

Pittsburgh is allowing the seventh-fewest yards per game and the third-fewest rush yards per game this season.

The Patriots will cross the pond this weekend to take on the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, on Sunday morning.

New England wide receiver A.J. Brown will travel with the team, head coach Mike Vrabel said. While this doesn't automatically mean he will play in Sunday's game, Vrabel noted it gives him the chance.

Brown has missed the Patriots' last two games due to a knee injury. The wide receiver has only played in three games for New England this season, as he missed the early part of the season because of a sprained ankle in Week 1.

The wide receiver has caught nine of his 20 targets for 101 yards. Brown has yet to score a touchdown this year.

Tuesday's trade deadline was highlighted by the return of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings.

Despite the move, on Wednesday, Minnesota head coach Kevin O'Connell wasn't ready to commit to Cousins as the starter this weekend against the Packers.

This could just be gamesmanship by O'Connell, but he told the media about Cousins starting: "I will say [we're] excited about the opportunity of spending every moment we can between now and then to get him comfortable and allow him to play for us this Sunday. That's what we're working towards, but also want to be fair to Kirk and make sure he feels good about it going to Lambeau Field."

Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur said in his Wednesday press conference that he was surprised that the Raiders didn't get more for Cousins. "I was surprised [the Raiders] didn't get more for him, quite honestly. I was shocked when I saw what they traded him for."

Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs may not end up on injured reserve despite needing surgery on his broken ring finger.

Jacobs, who is set to have that procedure later this week, could be back as soon as 2-3 weeks, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, who also reported that Green Bay will decide Saturday if IR is necessary.

The Packers play the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. But then they have a bye. There's a chance Jacobs returns for the following week's road game against the Los Angeles Rams.

The Chiefs will stick with Harrison Butker in Week 10, giving the kicker another chance to turn things around after weeks of struggles, head coach Andy Reid announced Wednesday.

After Sunday's win over the Jets, in which Butker missed another field goal attempt (a 51-yarder), Reid said that he would "look at everything" to assess whether it was time to move on. Evidently, Reid decided to stick with his long-time kicker.

Butker, who has spent his entire 10-year NFL career with the Chiefs, has seen his field goal accuracy crater this season. He's missed seven field goals in eight games so far this year, going 12-of-19 on attempts. That 63% completion rate is a noticeable dip from his previous decade of experience.

New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson will be back at practice Wednesday, albeit in a limited capacity while coming off a concussion, per ESPN's Rich Cimini.

Wilson was sidelined during last week's 35-12 road loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.

He absorbed a blow to the head from safety Jeremy Chinn late in a Week 8 defeat to the Las Vegas Raiders. Wilson then reported concussion symptoms the following Monday, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters.

Wilson has piled up 43 receptions, 527 receiving yards and 3 receiving touchdowns this season.

The Cleveland Browns are expected to turn back to quarterback Deshaun Watson in Week 10, according to The Athletic.

The move was expected, as reports emerged Monday saying Watson would start for the team after clearing concussion protocol.

Browns head coach Todd Monken shot down those rumors Monday, however, saying he had yet to make a decision on the team's starter in Week 10.

With Watson sidelined, Shedeur Sanders drew his first start of the 2026 season. He nearly led the Browns to an overtime win in that start.

Watson, who missed the contest due to a concussion, reportedly cleared league protocol Friday. Despite that, the was not active for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

The Dallas Cowboys have signed former Saints running back Kendre Miller to their practice squad, according to multiple reports.

Miller played sparingly in three-plus seasons as a backup for the Saints, tallying 656 rushing yards on 3.6 yards per carry in 27 appearances. The Saints released the former third-round pick on Saturday after signing Audric Estime off waivers from the Cleveland Browns.

With backup running back Tyler Goodson sidelined with a knee sprain, Miller adds a potential depth piece behind starter Javonte Williams.

Acquiring Kirk Cousins wasn't the only notable Vikings roster move on Tuesday.

Shortly after Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET NFL trade deadline, the Vikings announced that they have released wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. Per NFL insider Tom Pelissero, Beckham will re-sign with Minnesota's practice squad.

The transaction clears a spot on the 53-man roster that can make room for Cousins.

Beckham joined the Vikings after being released by the Giants three games into his return to New York. Beckham played in just one game for Minneosta, Monday's disastrous loss to the Bills that ultimately prompted them to trade for Cousins on Tuesday. He did not catch a pass for the Vikings.

The Ravens and Falcons pulled off a buzzer-beater trade right at the deadline.

Baltimore sent G Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 6th-round pick to Atlanta for C Ryan Neuzil, per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones.

Vorhees was a backup guard for the Ravens, while Neuzil was the Falcons' starting center.

Officiating – Officiating is always an x-factor in every game. Every crew officiates differently. Some call it tight, others let them play. #2701. Bruno Senna reveals plans to put Kimi Antonelli behind the wheel of Ayrton Senna's F1 car

Former Formula 1 driver Bruno Senna says he wants to give Kimi Antonelli the chance to drive one of Ayrton Senna's cars next year, after the 2026 world champion visited the family's estate in Brazil.

Antonelli arrived at the estate days after clinching his maiden F1 championship at the Mexican Grand Prix, becoming the youngest driver in the history of the series to win the title.

Speaking on F1's Beyond The Grid podcast, Bruno said the Mercedes driver barely wanted to get out of the Lotus 98T that his uncle raced in 1986.

"It was really, really fun to see him," he said. "We have the Lotus, the '86 car. We had him jump inside the car, and he didn't want to leave the car. You had the turbo boost knob, and he's exploring everything – having an anti-roll bar thing that you can change, and there's a gearstick."

Antonelli's love of the Lotus 98T gave Bruno the idea of having the Italian drive the car next year.

"This is something that was quite funny – I was talking [about] next year when Lotus or McLaren want to do something, we can try to organise for [him] to drive one of these cars because he fits really well in the car," he continued.

"You know, his height is perfect for it. His dad was like, 'I'm not sure if you can drive the manual car', and Kimi was like, 'sure I can!'"

In addition to sitting in the Lotus 98T, Antonelli also had some time on the go-kart track that Ayrton designed on the estate, where Bruno saw first-hand what the 20-year-old can do.

"Finally, we drove on the go-kart track that Ayrton designed," he added. "It was a really fun thing when I was a kid, and Kimi was incredible. He was so fast, so consistent. We had a fun time. I would say that I was slower because I'm 10kg heavier, but I think there's a bit more than that in it, to be honest! He was amazing.

"The track was very dirty, very full of stone. Kimi was able to create a groove, and he was able to stay within that groove so consistently. It was really impressive. He couldn't move 10cm off because then you don't even run wide – you go onto the grass and spin out because it was so dirty. It was a really cool experience and showed why he's a world champion."

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2695. 'It's forever': Lakers rookie Cameron Carr cherishing first NBA points

The son of former NBA dunk contest runner-up Chris Carr, Lakers rookie Cameron Carr envisioned his first NBA points coming on a lob. When asked before the draft in April, the first-round pick knew that if not on a sky-high alley-oop his first bucket would at least be something athletic.

He now gives himself half-credit for calling his shot.

The 21-year-old Lakers guard scored his first NBA points on a fastbreak dunk Monday in Atlanta, making the most of his opportunities during the Lakers' hot start.

Carr had two points and three rebounds in seven minutes and 19 seconds in the Lakers' win over the Atlanta Hawks in the first significant playing time of his professional career. The Lakers, who finish a three-game, four-day road trip in Milwaukee on Wednesday, have the top record in the NBA at 10-2 with a six-game winning streak.

Carr helped extend the Lakers' streak by bolstering a shorthanded lineup against the Hawks. The Lakers needed the rookie Monday when they were without Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (right finger sprain).

Three weeks into his NBA career, Carr, the 24th overall pick the Lakers traded up to acquire from the New York Knicks, said he is still nervous any time he subs into a game. Getting the first of what he hopes will be many NBA points helped settle his nerves.

Read more: What we've learned about the first-place Lakers

"Over time it's only going to grow, it's only going to get better," Carr said. "I'm only going to get more and more confident, so every time I get a chance to step out there, just show what I can do and of course show my talents through God's work."

The 6-foot-5 guard is a skilled scorer and an athletic marvel. He couldn't even touch the rim when, one summer, he begged his father, who was the runner-up in the 1997 dunk contest to Kobe Bryant, to teach him to dunk. He just needed one summer to master it. Carr set a single-season sophomore scoring record at Baylor last season and his 642 points rank fifth in program history regardless of class. An efficient shooter (37.4% from three in his final college season), Carr also led Baylor with 45 blocked shots.

Now in the NBA, defense is still where Carr can improve most, Lakers coach JJ Redick said. Although Carr is a talented offensive player, it is still difficult for young players to find their rhythm with limited playing time, Redick said. The Lakers staff has encouraged Carr to take advantage of stay-ready games against coaches and make the most of G League opportunities to get more reps. Carr had 13 points and four rebounds during the Coachella Valley Lakers' season opener on Friday.

"Just being patient, man," Carr said of his approach to the beginning of the season, "just putting my head down, working every day, knowing that I can be the best person I can be. And when my time, my name is called, just be ready."

Carr subbed into Monday's game with 3:35 remaining in the first quarter. The Lakers, trailing by two, soon flipped the game with 13 unanswered points to end the quarter. A steal by Luka Doncic with 1:44 remaining fueled the streak and the star point guard threw an outlet pass to Carr in transition, who collected the ball for an emphatic two-handed dunk.

Doncic dished out another assist after the game when he rushed to secure the game ball for Carr. The superstar said he wanted the rookie to remember his first NBA bucket.

"That's big time," Carr said Wednesday of Doncic's kind gesture. "Especially coming from him, that says a lot about who he is as a person and how he views this team."

Redick handed the game ball to Carr in the locker room after the win as teammates cheered. Carr broke the team huddle on the word "together." He plans to have everyone sign the ball before keeping it in a trophy case.

"There's no price on it," Carr said. "It's forever."

The Lakers swapped out two-way centers Tuesday, waiving Lawson Lovering and signing Carson Cooper, the team announced. Both previously played in the Memphis Grizzlies organization and Cooper made one NBA appearance for the Grizzlies after signing a two-way deal with the team.

Cooper didn't become a regular starter in college until his senior season, when he started all 35 games for Michigan State. The four-year Spartan averaged 11.1 points on 58.4% shooting with 7.1 rebounds, 1.5 assists and one block in his final season.

Lovering, who signed a two-way deal with the Lakers on Oct. 28, appeared in Lakers blowouts against Miami and Sacramento with a rebound and a block.

#2694. Phoenix Suns Will Continue Building Around Devin Booker After 11 Years

As it stands, the Phoenix Suns have yet to prove themselves as a Western Conference contender. After going 45-37 in 2025-26, they had ambitions of taking a step up in the Western Conference, only to start 4-6 this season.

As the Suns continue to struggle, star shooting guard Devin Booker's future has been questioned, sparking countless rumors across the NBA. This week, however, league insider Michael Scotto provided the latest intel on the Suns, confirming their commitment to build around Booker for the foreseeable future.

"From every indication I've gotten, the Phoenix Suns want to keep Devin Booker, and they want to make the team better around him," said Michael Scotto. "From Devin Booker, every indication I've gotten is that he still wants to be a Sun for life, ideally. He did an extension recently with them, and he's been the face of the franchise for a while now. For Phoenix right now, it's about trying to make the team better around him."

In the era of player empowerment, NBA teams have to try harder than ever to keep their stars, and the Suns are no exception. Since drafting shooting guard Devin Booker in 2015, they've tried to build around him, with varying degrees of success. As recently as 2021, they made the NBA Finals, but the Suns have been unable to replicate that formula after losing key stars like Kevin Durant and Bradley Beal.

This season, despite celebrated summer signings, the Suns are struggling to keep up with the top contenders. At 4-6, they are 11th in the Western Conference and considered underdogs to advance to the NBA playoffs. Despite this, the Suns remain committed to building around Booker, their leading star since 2015.

Drafted 13th overall, Booker has been the face of the Suns for years now, outlasting several star teammates, including Chris Paul and Kevin Durant. This season, through the first 10 games, Booker is averaging 25.1 points, 2.7 rebounds, 4.8 assists, and 1.0 steals on 48.3% shooting from the field. With those stats, Devin would net a valuable return in a trade, but the Suns aren't ready to test the market, despite being 4-6.

With team owner Mat Ishbia committed to immediate results, the Suns are more likely to make a win-now move around Booker than to trade him and start from scratch. Drafted 13th overall in 2015, Booker has been a reliable scorer for the Suns, averaging 24.6 points, 4.0 rebounds, 5.3 assists, 1.0 steal, and 0.3 blocks per game on 48.3% shooting.

The problem is, Phoenix has yet to meet expectations in the Booker era. Despite trying to stack the deck in their favor, the Suns have seen a sharp decline in the West, raising questions about Booker's future. But with both the Suns and Booker himself set on continuing their partnership, there's no question about what comes next for this team. At 11th in the West, the Suns are scrambling to improve their standing and keep Booker satisfied, but only time will tell how it pays off. At the very least, rival teams should know the Suns aren't ready to blow it up and trade all their best assets before February's deadline.

#2689. When Scott Boras' phone rings, agent quips: 'Just another owner begging to meet with Skubal'

LAS VEGAS (AP) — Scott Boras was 15 minutes into his annual pun-filled news conference at the general managers meetings when a cellphone rang in his pocket.

"Just another owner begging to meet with Skubal," baseball's most visible agent quipped Wednesday.

Boras represents about two dozen free agents in what Major League Baseball hopes is the last offseason without a salary cap. Tarik Skubal, a Boras client, could set a contract record for a pitcher.

Teams are negotiating to reach deals before an expected lockout starts Dec. 2.

"There's a clear intent on a group of players," said Boras, whose free agent clients include Randy Arozarena, Nick Martinez and Max Scherzer. "They're pursuing it aggressively."

MLB's five-year labor contract expires Dec. 1 at 12:59 p.m. EST and management is expected to immediately start the sport's 10th work stoppage since 1972.

On the day before the lockout began in 2021, there were 27 announced contracts that totaled more than $1.4 billion — include deals for Boras clients Corey Seager and Marcus Semien that accounted for $500 million.

Boras maintained veteran players are willing to sit out in order to fight off a cap, which owners have proposed for the first time since a 7 1/2-month strike in 1994 and '95.

"They are the ones that are the most aware," he said. "They are recipients of what others did for them and they are in great places in their lives and they're more than willing to share, contribute, aid and frankly stabilize the approach that the veterans took for them to apply to the young players of today."

He called management's proposal to increase the major league minimum salary to $900,000 a carrot.

"They're so repetitious. They are anticipated," he said. "Those are very de minimis advances, knowing the ask of what they want to take away."

He used the term "Reven-occhio" — wordplay on the children's story character Pinocchio, whose nose grows when he lies — to say MLB's claims economic change is needed are belied by private equity's investment in teams. He claimed a salary cap was "something that is going to create a true talent tyranny" and increase club equity value at a far higher rate than player salaries.

"The Broncos sell for $4.5 billion five years ago and the Seahawks sell for $9.6 billion," Boras said, citing approximate amount of those deals. "Over 100% increase in franchise value. What's the cap structure do for the players? And the reality of it is they're sitting there going with this modest increase of half that, 50%."

"The asset class of our game is documented throughout by genius owners, genius owners having the freedom, the ability under this system, to come in and advance their thoughts, to bring in the wherewithal for them to grow a franchise to its optimum," he said.

— "It's very clear that there is a dominant and strong Sku-Bull market."

— "Teams are not devoid of pursuing their championship fortunes and they understand there's only one Tarik card."

— "Teams have filled their tanks and they're all clearly ready for the Skubal dive."

#2687. Stephen Curry and Kevin Durant meet again as Warriors head to Houston

Back in the day, guys weren't supposed to be this good this late. Kareem was the exception everybody pointed to for decades, still putting up 23.4 a night and making All-NBA at 38. LeBron is the recent exception. Everybody else got the farewell tour, the rocking chair at the end of the bench, and the jersey ceremony.

If you've ever iced a rec-league knee after a Tuesday night run, take a good long look at Steph Curry and Kevin Durant tonight. While most 38-year olds are having to take a day off of work to go see their medical provider for their aching spines, these two are doing something most 25 year old hoopers can't do. As of Nov. 9, of the 38 players in the league averaging at least 20 points, only two were older than 35, and they'll be on the same floor in Houston. That's love of the game, plus years of cold tubs, film sessions, and a burning desire to dominate.

Tonight is the 41st time these two have faced each other. Both teams are 8-3, and both are coming off seasons that ended beneath them. The Warriors went 37-45 and lost to Phoenix in the play-in. Houston won 52 games and then fell to the Lakers in the first round with Durant hobbled. Golden State has won eight straight, and its offense ranks second in the league, one spot ahead of Houston's.

KD and Steph's legacies are tied together for good. They went from playoff rivals in 2016 to teammates in Oakland, where they won two titles and Durant took home both Finals MVPs. In Paris in 2024, with France still threatening an upset, Steph swung the ball to Durant at the top of the key, and KD handed it right back. Steph buried a fadeaway three over Nic Batum and Evan Fournier to put the U.S. up nine with 35 seconds left. As teammates they've proven at the highest level how to make sure each other gets the ball when it's their moment to shine. And nobody can seize the moment like these two hoopers can.

A crazy perspective on Curry now is the scoring he packs into the minutes he's got. He's averaging 30.6 points, with nights of 44 and 41 already. Through his first seven games, he was scoring 1.04 points per minute, a rate only Wilt Chamberlain, George Gervin, Luka Dončić and James Harden had topped that early in a season. Even Durant has noticed. Back in April he told NBA.com that Steph "got quicker and faster," a terrifying thought for the rest of the league.

What's ice cold about Durant nowadays is his level of control. His scoring is down to 21 a night, the lowest since his rookie year, but the possession still bends around him. He's a 6-foot-11 sculpture of a jump shot who sits No. 5 on the all-time scoring list, and he just put up 23 points, 12 rebounds and 8 assists on Denver.

That's the problem Golden State has to solve tonight. When Durant has the ball, every defender leans toward him, and teammates like the All-Star Alperen Şengün make you pay for leaning. He's averaging 21.3 points, 9.0 rebounds and 7.8 assists, and with Houston missing Clint Capela and Steven Adams, even more of the offense will run through those two. Watch whether Draymond can sit on Şengün's cuts and rolls without giving Durant a clean look. Golden State is still without Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody and Kristaps Porzingis. This morning's official report also has Gary Payton II out and Will Richard questionable.

Steph owns the playoff edge at 4-3, all from that 2016 comeback. Since Durant left the Warriors, he's 7-3 against Steph. Houston will take your lunch money in November, but April and May are another story, and the Warriors have five playoff series wins over the Rockets to prove it.

Savor this one. Two 38-year-olds are doing things the sport told us were impossible, and we get to watch it on a random Wednesday in November.
